newsitem.title: ITALY: Cargo plane crashes in Italy, 22 feared dead.
newsitem.headline: Cargo plane crashes in Italy, 22 feared dead.

text.p: At least 22 people were feared killed when a Russian-built Antonov cargo plane crashed on Tuesday while attempting to land at Turin airport in northwest Italy, rescue services said.

The plane, which had come from Moscow, appeared to have aborted a first attempt to land at Turin's Caselle airport and stalled as it prepared to make a fresh approach to the runway, an official at the local prefecture said.
He said he believed there had been 24 people on board the aircraft. Other reports put the number of people at 20 to 23.
"At least 22 people are dead. They were all on board," a fire service spokesman said.
Initial reports had said the plane crashed on take-off.
The plane struck a farm building and appeared to have damaged other buildings before it came to rest in a road close to a cemetery in the village of San Francesco del Campo.
A spokesman at the Di Cirie hospital near Turin told Reuters injured people were being rushed to its casualty centre.
A doctor at the hospital said: "The situation is critical and many injured have been brought in."
It was not clear whether there were had been any injured on the ground. Helicopters were also flown to the scene to ferry casualties to the hospital.
No details of the precise type of Antonov, its route, its owners or its cargo were immediately available.
A local council employee in San Francesco del Campo said she had heard two explosions and later saw the plane lying in a road. She said the plane was still in one piece.
A reporter with state broadcaster RAI said firemen had clambered into the fuselage and had found survivors on board.
